title: Reward Budgeting Reduces Premature Convergence in Reinforcement Learning for LLM Reasoning
claim: As training proceeds, policy entropy collapses while validation accuracy rises slowly and then plateaus or declines, showing premature convergence.
layout: single dual-axis line plot, entropy left and accuracy right, over training steps
description: A single line chart with a shared x-axis for training step, from 0 to 1000. The left y-axis shows Entropy (1 to 7), and the right y-axis shows Validation Accuracy (0.06 to 0.11). A blue noisy line for entropy starts near 7 and falls steadily to about 1.3. An orange noisy line for validation accuracy climbs quickly from about 0.053 and then rises slowly to a peak of about 0.11 near step 840. After that it drops to about 0.096 by step 1000. A legend at top right labels the two series and overlaps the orange line. The plot has grey gridlines and the two lines cross on the left. The eye goes first to the opposing trends of the two curves.
caption: Average training entropy and validation accuracy across 12 Llama3.2-3B-Instruct runs.
abstract: RL for LLM reasoning often plateaus early as its policy sharpens. Policy entropy is studied as both a diagnostic and a control signal, but increasing it alone does not reliably change the eventual plateau in our experiments. We analyze RL's implicit target policy using a sharpness factor $Îº$ and effective counterpart $Îº_{\mathrm{eff}}$ that describe how reward or advantage gaps translate into probability-ratio gaps. We introduce reward budgeting, a plug-in advantage construction assigning a fixed total reward budget to each prompt. For binary rewards and independent on-policy rollouts, its expected unclipped score-function update is the exact gradient of a finite-$G$ concave objective with diminishing returns; its advantage gap decreases as more rollouts become correct. For general rewards, a shifted log-mean interpretation holds asymptotically under the stated regularity conditions. On Qwen3-8B and Llama3.2-3B-Instruct, reward budgeting consistently improves RL baselines, with gains up to +12.50 on AMC23 and +10.00 on AIME24 and AIME25. These results support an update-dynamics view of premature convergence and substantial gains without explicitly preserving entropy. Code is available at https://github.com/Qwen-Applications/RewardBudget.
